solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Contact Queen following introduction to prime minister

indicators.note: the contact-and-queen pieces come after the opening letter in the answer
the introduction to a word is its opening letter, here of the word prime

parts.note: to contact someone is to reach them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone gets in touch with the monarch after a word from the prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime minister' looks like one phrase, but 'prime' gives its first letter and 'minister' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion delivers sermons, so a preacher is one kind of minister.

clue.text: Kitty in a puddle

definitions.meaning: a kitty is a shared fund of money

explanation.definitionFit: Both a shared pot of stakes and a small body of standing water go by this one word.

clue.text: Get in touch after divorced spouse cast out of Church

indicators.note: the touch piece comes after the former-spouse piece in the answer

parts.note: a former husband or wife is an ex
to communicate with someone is to get in touch

explanation.surface: A former spouse makes contact once they have been expelled by the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: Excommunication is the formal expulsion of a member from the Church and its sacraments.

clue.text: Tool for slicing item of junk mail was put into reverse

parts.note: a circular is a leaflet sent out to many addresses at once

indicators.note: the word was is turned round so that it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A tool that cuts through a piece of unwanted post was driven backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A power tool with a toothed spinning disc used for cutting timber and other material.

clue.text: Mistakes unusually rare: thanks!

indicators.note: the letters of rare are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: ta is an informal British word for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone thanks a writer whose errors are, unusually, few and far between.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural for errors, used for a list of printing corrections in a book.

clue.text: Flower discovered in Fair Isle

indicators.note: the letters are found lying inside the words Fair Isle

explanation.surface: A bloom is found growing on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle is a remote Scottish island, famous for its knitwear patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden plant with showy blooms, often blue or purple.

clue.text: Milestone to one side of alleyway read out

indicators.note: the phrase built is spoken, giving words that are pronounced the same but spelt differently

parts.note: one side is right, alleyway is passage, giving right of passage

explanation.surface: A marker stone beside a lane has its inscription spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: RIGHT (one side) + OF + PASSAGE (alleyway) is pronounced the same as the answer's first word RITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony or event marking an important transition in life is a milestone in that life.

clue.text: Miss start of show despite being organised

indicators.note: the start of the word show is its opening letter
the letters of despite are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone misses the start of a show even though it has been well organised.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge or avoid something, like a blow or an issue, is to miss it deliberately.

clue.text: Film award for Mr Hammerstein?

definitions.meaning: the Academy Award statuette is nicknamed this
the lyricist Hammerstein of Rodgers and Hammerstein had this first name

explanation.surface: A film prize is given to the famous lyricist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette and the lyricist Hammerstein share this name.

clue.text: Alleged grass gets put inside

indicators.note: the word put goes inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside grass

explanation.surface: A supposed informer, a grass, ends up being sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like slang for an informer; here it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reputed is generally said or believed to be so, without proof, just like alleged.

clue.text: Group of lions added to Ms Adamson's personal delight

parts.note: a pride is the collective name for lions
and is a word that adds one thing to another
Joy Adamson wrote Born Free about raising lions

explanation.surface: Joy Adamson, who raised lions, takes delight in a group of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Joy Adamson was the author of Born Free, about the lioness Elsa.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something or someone that a person is very proud of and cherishes.

clue.text: Towering form of ominous aunt

indicators.note: a new form is made from the letters of ominous aunt

explanation.surface: A menacing aunt looms over everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something huge and high like a range of peaks is towering in scale.

clue.text: Cook focuses hard for his assistant?

indicators.note: to cook figures is to rearrange them, so these letters are cooked

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils

explanation.surface: A chef concentrates hard on behalf of the kitchen helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the definition, but it is the anagram signal; 'his' then refers back to a cook, making the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The second-in-command in a professional kitchen works under the head chef as deputy.

clue.text: Some jocularity concerning sightseers, perhaps

indicators.note: only some of the letters of jocularity are taken, lying inside it

explanation.surface: A tour guide cracks jokes with the visiting tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sightseers' is a playful name for eyes, the organs that see sights.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the eyes, which are whimsically the things that see sights.

clue.text: Meet eccentric around place or house of worship

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the place abbreviation
eccentric means odd, so the letters of meet go askew

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Odd folk gather around some spot or a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' gives TEME; 'Meet' looks like a verb but is anagram fodder, and 'or' simply links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a building dedicated to religious worship, especially in non-Christian faiths.

clue.text: Actor quietly put on coat

indicators.note: in a down answer the quiet letter sits on top of the coat word

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
a coat of paint is a layer

explanation.surface: A performer silently slips on a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is an old word for a stage performer, as in Shakespeare's players.

clue.text: Keep mum in supportive braces for lower-leg complaint

parts.note: sh is the call to keep quiet
splints are rigid supports strapped to an injured limb

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay quiet while wearing supports for a leg problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful inflammation along the front of the lower leg, common among runners.

clue.text: Like the present given by a little sibling

parts.note: sis is the short form of sister

explanation.surface: A gift handed over by a younger brother or sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift; here it is the present state of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Sold or left in its existing state, exactly like it is now.

clue.text: Leader means to make progress

parts.note: a head is the leader of a school or group
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: A chief intends to move things forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, a method.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward movement or advance, as in the idiom make headway.

clue.text: Girl's legwear

definitions.meaning: belonging to a girl called Jean

explanation.definitionFit: Denim trousers share their spelling with the possessive of the girl's name Jean.

clue.text: Release without charge

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to liberate a captive and costing nothing at all.

clue.text: Cape on Lady Jane displaying dull quality

indicators.note: the cape word is placed on, i.e. after, the lady's surname

parts.note: Lady Jane Grey was the nine-day queen of England in 1553
ness is a word for a headland, as in Loch Ness or Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A headland portrait of Lady Jane Grey looks rather dreary.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Jane Grey was briefly Queen of England in 1553.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of colour or interest, the state of being drab and dreary, is a dull quality.
